skill.title: fault_mode_string_payload_extraction_off_by_one_due_to_regex_and_slicing_v1
skill.trigger: Reports of parsed string values containing unexpected extra/missing characters for escape sequences; traces show a single helper that extracts payload (names like _get_payload, get_payload, or regex matches in tree/token classes).
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: regex-based string payload extraction that captures surrounding quotes and payload in groups, combined with slicing of the captured group, can be off-by-one and include an extra leading/trailing character. Observable signals: (1) reported parsed string leaf.value contains an unexpected extra char at the start or end when escape sequences are present; (2) a single small helper (e.g., _get_payload) implements both the regex and final slice; (3) callers decode/unescape payload (unicode_escape/escape_decode) and surface decode errors or incorrect values. Root-location bias: tree/Leaf string helpers (tree.py) implementing regex extraction. Confusable alternatives: tokenization step producing different token boundaries or downstream decoder mis-decoding an otherwise-correct payload — always inspect both extractor and decoder callers. Anti-patterns: slicing using hard-coded indices without verifying group contents, assuming group(2) excludes the opening quote, or trusting DOTALL matches to isolate payload boundaries.

edit_history.rationale: Existing fault-mode candidates pertained to validators or missing initialization and do not capture the off-by-one/regex-group slicing pattern found here. This case provides a clear, reusable fault-mode: regex/group capture plus slicing that leaves an extra char in payloads.

Observable signals: errors saying 'position does not exist within node' or None for positions at exact child.start_pos; code patterns to inspect include comparisons like 'position <= element.end_pos' vs 'position < element.start_pos', hard-coded lower bounds, and midpoint calculations like int((lower+upper)/2) vs ceil variants. Preferred fixes: make inclusive/exclusive semantics explicit, choose midpoint rounding consistent with recursion indices (floor vs ceil), and add unit tests for positions equal to element.start_pos and element.end_pos. Confusable alternatives: bugs in tokenization or wrong start_pos values — quickly rule those out by printing element.start_pos and element.end_pos for the failing node.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge: If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

edit_history.rationale: Multiple cases (several alive-progress cards and a moto case) show a recurring retrieval/operational bias: empty or sparse repo search results lead agents to fall back to priors or to overweight lexical parser signals. Capturing a cross-dimensional general skill will make retrieval behavior explicit, reduce misranking, and guide conservative fallback heuristics.

skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge: If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

edit_history.rationale: Multiple cases (several alive-progress cards and a moto case) show a recurring retrieval/operational bias: empty or sparse repo search results lead agents to fall back to priors or to overweight lexical parser signals. Capturing a cross-dimensional general skill will make retrieval behavior explicit, reduce misranking, and guide conservative fallback heuristics.

skill.title: Check indexing, boundary inclusivity, argument order, and add lightweight position-reporting tests
skill.trigger: Triggered when reported coordinates, slices, merged lists, or token positions are incorrect or inconsistent; also when fixes/patches touch start_pos/end_pos/indexing, slice endpoints, midpoint logic, or merge loops.
skill.knowledge: Common root causes for incorrect coordinates or payloads: (1) tuple-index swaps or misordered arguments when assembling reports, (2) off-by-one in regex group extraction and slice endpoints, (3) binary-search/traversal mixing inclusive/exclusive comparisons or biased midpoints, (4) merge loops that combine neighbors while deleting elements (delete-shift bugs). Practical checklist: reproduce a minimal example; inspect all index and slice expressions and argument orders; verify inclusive/exclusive comparisons in traversal/search code; check midpoint computation and rounding; examine loops that mutate lists while iterating (consider reversed iteration or index sets); add or run small unit tests that assert both line and column values for produced tokens/Issues to catch regressions early. When instrumenting, prefer lightweight position-reporting assertions in unit tests or short repro harnesses that exercise both typical and boundary positions (exact child.start_pos and end_pos).
anti_patterns: Blaming decoders or upstream producers before checking extraction slices/indices and the immediate assembler.
Ignoring midpoint/inclusivity details in search/traversal logic.
Assuming merged-list loops are safe without reasoning about deletion order and index shifts.
Not adding tests that assert both line and column information when diagnostics are positional.

edit_history.rationale: Multiple parso cases demonstrate a recurring, high-impact class of bugs caused by off-by-one, tuple-index swaps, midpoint rounding, slice endpoints, and list mutation while iterating. skill.title: fault_mode_inverted_comparison_and_parameter_swap_in_numeric_mapping_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when numeric-scaling or calibration code produces globally inverted outputs (high inputs map to low outputs and vice versa) or canonical edge inputs (negative, zero) return zero/None instead of a documented bootstrap/default; diffs or code show clamp/limit lines, comparator operators, or min/max constants near the mapping math.
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: a polarity inversion in numeric mapping arises when clamps, comparator directions, or the constants used in mapping arithmetic are swapped. Common concrete mistakes: (1) using min where max was intended (or vice versa) when clamping parameters; (2) dividing/multiplying by the wrong clamped value (e.g., 100. / min(...) vs 100. / max(...)); (3) flipped branch comparators (<= vs <) that change which branch handles the edge-case; (4) returning min_fps where max_fps should be returned and vice versa. Observable signals: canonical edge-case tests (negative, zero, very large) produce wrong sentinel values (e.g., 0.0 instead of documented bootstrap), and high inputs map to the low bound. When you see these signals, inspect clamp lines and the immediate math that computes factors, then verify comparator directions and which constants are added to or multiplied by the factor. Confusable alternatives: off-by-one loops or generator-direction inversions — those usually produce ordering/count problems rather than numeric polarity inversion for continuous inputs.

Existing weak fault-mode candidates were about generator or cycle inversion (not the same numeric polarity bug). Creating a focused fault-mode skill captures the transferable lesson for future numeric-scaling regressions.

If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. skill.title: fault_mode_local_variable_used_before_assignment_reordered_late_initialization_v1
skill.trigger: NameError or UnboundLocalError naming a variable that appears in the same function but no obvious assignment before use; diffs that remove or move a call that previously assigned a helper variable (e.g., get_object).
skill.knowledge:
Fault-mode: local variable referenced before its initialization due to reordering or accidental deletion of its initializer. Observable signals: NameError/UnboundLocalError pointing to a local name inside a function; nearby lines show expected initializer calls (e.g., get_object/get_bucket) either absent or moved below the usage; ground-truth patches often reintroduce or restore the initializer. Root-location bias: the function body where the variable should be created (helpers invoking get_* or lookups). Confusable alternatives: missing global attribute vs. local initializer removed — check whether the name is assigned anywhere in the scope before use.

High-confidence signal: UnboundLocalError frequently follows a refactor that relocated an initializer below its first use — for example, moving the assignment between two loops or branches. When a local is used in multiple blocks, check diffs for deleted/moved assignment lines between those blocks.

Add: High-confidence subpattern — when a local initializer is referenced in multiple sequential usage blocks (e.g., two for-loops or separate branches) and a refactor moved the initializer to lie between those blocks, the first block may use the name before assignment. Detect by scanning for repeated loops/branches that reference the same local and verifying the initializer occurs before every usage. Example: QRCode.setup_type_number uses 'bits' in two loops; a moved assignment caused UnboundLocalError.

Add: Subpattern — when an optional parameter is defaulted (e.g., fs = fs or localfs) and that defaulting or a subsequent derived assignment (e.g., root_dir = fs.abspath(root)) is removed or guarded, derived locals can remain uninitialized for some call-site values (fs=None). Detect by checking for optional-parameter defaulting lines near the top of a function and verifying derived locals are always assigned regardless of parameter branches.

Observable signals: error messages naming the missing attribute/method; ground-truth diffs that delete a 'def name(' block or change its name; empty grep results for the expected symbol combined with a patch that removes the symbol. Confusable alternatives: return-type regressions or missing initialization—distinguish by checking whether the symbol definition itself is absent or altered in the diff. Check the repository diff/patch for removed 'def <name>(' hunks in the internal class and for facade properties that construct or proxy to that internal instance.

skill.trigger: Reports of TypeError from string operations in parser/tree code or issue text mentioning None/prefix/indent errors in parser wrappers; diffs that set public attributes to None or change default types in __init__.
skill.knowledge:
Fault mode: wrapper/initializer leaves public or tree-facing fields uninitialized or set to None (or otherwise wrong type) instead of canonical defaults (e.g., '' for textual prefixes, 0/[] for counters/lists). Observable signals: TypeError on string concatenation/slicing in tree traversal methods, grep matches for `prefix` assignments, patch diffs that change __init__ assignments for module/prefix/indents. Root-location bias: wrapper class __init__ and reset/constructor helpers; symptom-location bias: tree methods that concatenate prefixes (e.g., _remove_endmarker, finish, add_parsed_nodes). Confusable alternatives: upstream tokenizer producing unexpected empty prefix — confirm by inspecting token objects and their `prefix` fields. Anti-patterns: setting textual defaults to None, reusing other object's attribute directly without validating its type.

Add: Also watch for wrappers that should forward or expose underlying parser public fields (e.g., self.stack). A missing forward/assignment in __init__ (or not exposing a property delegating to an internal parser) will produce AttributeError at use sites even if internal parser instances are later created.

Add: When a wrapper implements attribute delegation (e.g., via __getattr__) a missing/wrong initializer for the delegate (e.g., assigning self._stream = None or omitting assignment) will surface as AttributeError at call sites — prioritize checking wrapper __init__ and recent diffs that touch the delegated field.

skill.title: project_type_parser_or_compiler_frontend_position_propagation_v1
skill.trigger: Bug reports about incorrect line/column coordinates in parser frontends or when error positions appear systematically shifted; grep shows many 'start_pos' mentions across tokenizer, tree, prefix, and normalizer.
skill.knowledge:
Project-type lesson: In parser/lexer frontends, source coordinates are produced by the tokenizer and then propagated and possibly transformed by token -> Leaf/Node constructors, prefix-handling (split_prefix), and tree start_pos accessors before being consumed by error-reporting/normalizer code. When positions are incorrect, prioritize files and functions that (1) produce token.start_pos (tokenize_lines), (2) assign token start_pos to leaf/node constructors (parser.convert_leaf / tree constructors), (3) compute prefix start positions (split_prefix/PrefixPart), and (4) read node.start_pos for issue assembly (ErrorFinder/normalizer). Confusable alternatives (e.g., wrong AST shapes) can be ruled out quickly by printing representative token.start_pos and leaf.start_pos values. Ranking bias: hunt upstream (tokenizer) and at explicit start_pos transforms before editing high-level error messages.

Add: For parser/front-end projects, explicitly inspect EndMarker and prefix-remainder code paths: functions that split or reassign leaf.prefix (e.g., _remove_endmarker), EndMarker construction (self.prefix + self._prefix_remainder), and node-copy/insert logic that concatenates prefixes are high-value locations when reported problems mention BOM, shifted positions, or unexpected error leaves. Pay special attention to split_lines usage and any code that decrements or slices prefix lengths (BOM branches).

skill.title: fault_mode_string_payload_extraction_off_by_one_due_to_regex_and_slicing_v1
skill.trigger: Reports of parsed string values containing unexpected extra/missing characters for escape sequences; traces show a single helper that extracts payload (names like _get_payload, get_payload, or regex matches in tree/token classes).
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: regex-based string payload extraction that captures surrounding quotes and payload in groups, combined with slicing of the captured group, can be off-by-one and include an extra leading/trailing character. Observable signals: (1) reported parsed string leaf.value contains an unexpected extra char at the start or end when escape sequences are present; (2) a single small helper (e.g., _get_payload) implements both the regex and final slice; (3) callers decode/unescape payload (unicode_escape/escape_decode) and surface decode errors or incorrect values. Root-location bias: tree/Leaf string helpers (tree.py) implementing regex extraction. Confusable alternatives: tokenization step producing different token boundaries or downstream decoder mis-decoding an otherwise-correct payload — always inspect both extractor and decoder callers. Anti-patterns: slicing using hard-coded indices without verifying group contents, assuming group(2) excludes the opening quote, or trusting DOTALL matches to isolate payload boundaries.

edit_history.rationale: Existing fault-mode candidates pertained to validators or missing initialization and do not capture the off-by-one/regex-group slicing pattern found here. This case provides a clear, reusable fault-mode: regex/group capture plus slicing that leaves an extra char in payloads.
evidence: parso/python/tree.py: String._get_payload uses re.search(r'''('{3}|\"{3}|'|\")(.*)$''', self.value) and then returns match.group(2)[:-len(match.group(1))].
Ground-truth patch: return match.group(2)[1:-len(match.group(1))] — adding [1:] removes an extra leading char included by group(2).
errors._StringChecks calls leaf._get_payload() then codecs.unicode_escape_decode; a wrong payload will produce decoding problems or include unexpected characters in leaf.value.

skill.knowledge:
Title: removed_or_simplified_parameter_and_return_shape_regression_in_emulator

Trigger: Tests or public-client calls for an API operation (list_permissions, list/describe) no longer return expected filtered results after recent edits or refactors; repository is an API-emulator with responses.py and backend model classes.

Knowledge: Refactor regressions commonly occur when a backend method's signature or return shape is simplified/changed and the responses layer or tests still expect the previous parameter/return contract. Observable signals:
- Method signatures shorten or drop parameters that were previously used for filtering (e.g., def list_permissions(self, catalog_id) replacing def list_permissions(self, catalog_id, principal=None, resource=None, resource_type=None)).
- The backend begins returning internal collections or backend objects instead of externally-formed lists/dicts (return-shape mismatch).
- Tests exercise filtered/listed responses (e.g., Resource={"DataLocation": {...}}) but get unfiltered or raw objects.

Root-location bias: prioritize recent edits to the suspect backend method (signature, removed helper classes/DTOs, replaced resource wrappers) and the responses->backend call site that constructs the resource/parameters. Check for:
1) signature changes that let filtering parameters be ignored,
2) removed or renamed resource wrapper classes (ListPermissionsResource*),
3) changed return expression (return self.grants[cid] vs return [p.to_external_form()]) and missing conversion to external form.

Confusable alternatives: missing internal state population or serializer bugs — distinguish by verifying whether the backend ever received/used the filtering args or if the backend now ignores them because signature or call-site was changed.

Ranking bias: elevate fixes that restore parameter passing, restore explicit conversion to external return form, or reintroduce the resource wrapper over unrelated cosmetic renames.
anti_patterns: Assuming missing results are only due to missing model population without checking for signature/return-shape regressions.
Stopping investigation at responses.py when the root cause is a backend signature/return-form change.

Title: inspect_signature_and_return_shape_regression_after_refactor

Trigger: After recent edits or failing tests, an API-emulator operation stops applying filters or returns raw/unexpected objects.

Knowledge (strategy):
- Step 1: Open responses.py and locate the handler for the failing API (e.g., list_permissions). Record what resource/parameters the response constructs and passes to the backend (resource wrappers, nested dicts).
- Step 2: Open the corresponding backend method (e.g., LakeFormationBackend.list_permissions). Compare its current signature with the call-site: ensure it still accepts the same parameters (principal, resource, resource_type) and that those parameters are used by filtering helpers.

Ranking bias: Rank candidate fixes that (a) restore parameter passing between responses and backend, (b) restore resource wrapper/DTOs or explicit conversion to external forms, and (c) fix return-shape mismatches above cosmetic renames.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

edit_history.rationale: Multiple cases (several alive-progress cards and a moto case) show a recurring retrieval/operational bias: empty or sparse repo search results lead agents to fall back to priors or to overweight lexical parser signals. Capturing a cross-dimensional general skill will make retrieval behavior explicit, reduce misranking, and guide conservative fallback heuristics.

skill.title: fault_mode_inverted_condition_in_descriptor_set_calls_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when a property assignment yields the wrong forwarded argument (e.g., user assigns non-None but delegate receives None) or when diffs show conditional branches in a descriptor's __set__/__get__ that appear to swap/negate forwarding.
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: Inverted-branch or swapped-argument in descriptor forwarding. Observable signal: property assignment (instance.prop = value) results in the delegate/handler being called with the wrong argument (often None) or the opposite value. Root-location bias: descriptor classes implementing __set__ / __get__ (and any wrapper that invokes the result of __get__ to handle assignments). Diagnostic preference: open the descriptor's __set__ and compare the condition used to decide what to pass to the delegate and the exact argument expression forwarded. Confusable alternatives: missing initialization of the delegate attribute, or delegate returning None — but those produce None because the delegate is None/absent, whereas inverted forwarding passes an explicit wrong literal/variable (e.g., None) when a non-None input exists. Ranking bias: for property-assignment misbehavior raise the rank of descriptor __set__ implementations and of tests/repro that show the delegate call args.
anti_patterns: Assuming the bug is in caller code rather than inspecting the descriptor forwarding logic first.
Treating missing delegate initialization as the only cause when a concrete wrong-literal (e.g., explicit None) is being forwarded.

edit_history.rationale: The ground-truth patch demonstrates a concise, reusable fault pattern: a descriptor's __set__ contains an inverted condition that forwards None instead of the provided value. This is a distinct fault-mode (inverted forwarding/polarity bug in descriptors) not captured precisely by existing fault-mode skills, so creating a dedicated fault-mode skill is preferable to mixing into broader constructor/initializer transformation skills.
evidence: Ground-truth patch: __set__ originally called self.__get__(obj)(value) but was changed to an inverted conditional that calls with None when value is not None (inverted argument forwarding).
Problem statement + repro: assigning instance.assignable = 3 caused underlying mock to be called with None (call(None)) instead of call(3).
edit_history.risk: Low-to-moderate: could overpromote descriptor code in repositories where descriptors are rare; mitigated by the trigger limiting application to property-assignment symptoms.

skill.knowledge: Strategy: prioritize finding descriptor definitions and their __set__/__get__ code when property-assignment symptoms occur. Steps/priors: (1) grep for class definitions that define __set__ or __get__ and for places where descriptors are instantiated on classes; (2) open the descriptor's __set__ and __get__ to inspect conditional logic and exact forwarded arguments (look for reversed conditions like 'if value is not None: forward None'); (3) compare the argument expression used in the forwarded call to the original incoming parameter (watch for swapped variables or explicit literals); (4) if repository search fails to find named symbols mentioned in the report, still attempt pattern-based search for '__set__', 'descriptor', or assignments of callables via member names and surface that you are doing a pattern search fallback. Ranking bias: boost candidates that define __set__/__get__ or that contain forwarding calls to stored delegates when repro shows wrong call-args. Confusable alternatives: delegate not initialised — rule out by checking whether the code forwards an explicit literal/variable (indicating logic error) vs. forwarding to a None delegate (indicating initialization problem).
anti_patterns: Stopping at a surface symptom (None observed) without checking whether the code explicitly forwards the wrong literal/variable.
Relying solely on name-based search when descriptor names are missing from the snapshot — use pattern-based search for '__set__' and 'def __get__' as a fallback.

skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).

skill.title: fault_mode_swapped_return_or_argument_order_in_presentation_helpers_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when animations/spinners render swapped/garbled frames and diffs or patch contexts show tuple unpacking/order changes, swapped return order, reversed step/sign assignments, or off-by-one slicing edits in framing/decoration helpers.
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: Swapped-return / misordered-tuple-unpacking and inverted polarity in presentation helpers. Description: presentation or framing helpers may accidentally swap the order of returned or yielded elements (e.g., returning (right, content) instead of (content, right)), invert boolean/step polarity (e.g., step sign or 'right' flag), or miscompute slice endpoints (off-by-one) — all of which change which glyphs become content vs border or reverse/garble frame sequences. Observable signals: repro shows frames swapped/garbled; diffs show reordered tuple unpacking or swapped assignment in decorators, reversed argument order in tuple-building, or arithmetic changes to copies/length/step. Root-location bias: wrapper/decorator functions that call lower-level producers and unpack returns, frame-generator factories, and sliding-window boundary arithmetic. Confusable alternatives: generator-bounding issues (zip with finite range) or initializer mutation — distinguish by inspecting return/unpack sites and sign/polarity of step/boolean parameters.

edit_history.rationale: The ground-truth patch shows repeated mistakes of swapped tuple unpacking/return order and boundary arithmetic changes (e.g., right, content = fn(...) instead of content, right; step polarity flip; slicing length adjustments). This is a distinct, transferable fault-mode (presentation helpers returning elements in the wrong order or using inverted step/signs) that is not cleanly covered by the retrieved fault-mode candidates, so creating a focused new skill is warranted.

Patch context: extract_fill_graphemes changed order of default/text tuple construction and swapped generator element selection
Patch context: static_sliding_window had step assignment polarity swapped and slicing length adjusted (off-by-one changes)
Reported repro showing frames in wrong order/garbled output
edit_history.risk: Medium — risk of overgeneralizing from a few cases where order was swapped; mitigated by strict trigger that looks for explicit unpack/return/order inversion signals.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.

Ranking bias: when trigger occurs, boost files where the symbol is referenced in isinstance and files where it was defined or recently changed.
anti_patterns: Assuming the NameError always means the caller is wrong; often the definition was removed in the same function.
Stopping at downstream callers: prefer checking local assignments and recent diffs before chasing consumers.

skill.title: fault_mode_removed_or_renamed_public_method_v1
skill.trigger: Reports of AttributeError for an expected public method on an object ("object has no attribute 'X'") or diffs/patches showing method lines removed/renamed.
skill.knowledge:
Fault-mode: a public method was removed or renamed during refactor (or its body deleted), producing immediate AttributeError at call sites. Observable signals: error messages naming the missing attribute/method; ground-truth diffs that delete a 'def name(' block or change its name; empty grep results for the expected symbol combined with a patch that removes the symbol. Root-location bias: the file/module that previously housed lightweight helpers (util, data, encoders) and the commit/patch metadata (deleted/modified hunks). Confusable alternatives: return-type regressions or missing initialization—distinguish by checking whether the symbol definition itself is absent or altered in the diff. Anti-pattern: chasing only caller-side changes when the correct fix is restoring/reconciling a removed method; always inspect the patch/diff or VCS history when searches fail to find the symbol.

Also include refactor-deletion in internal/private delegate classes as a high-confidence signal: when a public facade delegates to an internal/private instance (e.g., DVCFileSystem -> cached _DVCFileSystem), deleted or renamed def blocks inside that internal class will produce AttributeError at runtime. Check the repository diff/patch for removed 'def <name>(' hunks in the internal class and for facade properties that construct or proxy to that internal instance.

Add: Treat simultaneous AttributeError failures for many methods on the same class as a high-confidence removal/rename event. Practical signals: (1) multiple distinct method names produce AttributeError on the same type instance; (2) VCS/patch hunks that delete several 'def <name>(' blocks in the class file; (3) factories/loaders that construct the class (e.g. loads_from/create_stage) present in the repo. When these signals appear, recommend inspecting the class definition file and recent diffs before investigating callers.

Ranking bias: boost files that define the class and its loaders when this trigger occurs. Confusable alternatives: missing-attribute due to dynamic attribute creation or delegation; distinguish by presence/absence of def blocks in the class file and by diff evidence.
anti_patterns: Stopping at the first caller-site or assuming a single-name typo; avoid prioritizing downstream callers before checking class def and diff.
Treating a single missing helper as equivalent to multi-method deletion; require multiple missing-method signals or diff evidence to trigger this strategy.

When positions are incorrect, prioritize files and functions that (1) produce token.start_pos (tokenize_lines), (2) assign token start_pos to leaf/node constructors (parser.convert_leaf / tree constructors), (3) compute prefix start positions (split_prefix/PrefixPart), and (4) read node.start_pos for issue assembly (ErrorFinder/normalizer). Confusable alternatives (e.g., wrong AST shapes) can be ruled out quickly by printing representative token.start_pos and leaf.start_pos values. Ranking bias: hunt upstream (tokenizer) and at explicit start_pos transforms before editing high-level error messages.

Add: For parser/front-end projects, explicitly inspect EndMarker and prefix-remainder code paths: functions that split or reassign leaf.prefix (e.g., _remove_endmarker), EndMarker construction (self.prefix + self._prefix_remainder), and node-copy/insert logic that concatenates prefixes are high-value locations when reported problems mention BOM, shifted positions, or unexpected error leaves. Pay special attention to split_lines usage and any code that decrements or slices prefix lengths (BOM branches).

skill.title: fault_mode_rule_get_node_returns_adjacent_leaf_instead_of_original_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when diagnostics are mispositioned and grep/read_file shows get_node implementations calling get_next_leaf(), node.next, or splitting prefix to choose the returned node.
skill.knowledge:
Fault-mode: rule_get_node_returns_adjacent_leaf_instead_of_original

When a normalizer/ErrorFinder rule implements get_node and returns an adjacent leaf/node (e.g., node.get_next_leaf(), node.next, or the result of splitting a leaf.prefix) instead of the original node, diagnostic start_pos and end_pos will be shifted relative to the reported construct. Observable signals: diagnostics consistently point to the next token/leaf, test reproductions that compare node.start_pos vs node.get_next_leaf().start_pos, and get_node implementations that call get_next_leaf() or split_prefix. Root-location bias: Rule.get_node implementations in normalizer/error modules. Confusable alternatives: tokenization or prefix handling bugs — confirm by printing both the original node.start_pos and the candidate return value's start_pos before editing. Anti-patterns: editing message text or Issue position assembly before verifying get_node semantics.
anti_patterns: Assuming the base Rule.get_node semantics when subclasses override get_node without inspection.
Fixing issue text or deduplication logic before checking get_node return expressions.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.

Add: When repository search and file reads return no matches but the bug report names specific files or functions, explicitly mark localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend: (1) checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the supplied patch, (2) surfacing the fact that ranked functions were chosen from the reporter's names rather than repository evidence, and (3) deprioritizing lexical matches until the snapshot/patch is reconciled.

Addendum: when repository searches/reads return no matches but a supplied patch/diff or patch context is present, prefer using the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence (package/module names, file paths, and modified code) and explicitly label any subsequent localization as a 'fallback-to-priors' result if the snapshot and patch disagree.
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

edit_history.rationale: Multiple cases (several alive-progress cards and a moto case) show a recurring retrieval/operational bias: empty or sparse repo search results lead agents to fall back to priors or to overweight lexical parser signals. Capturing a cross-dimensional general skill will make retrieval behavior explicit, reduce misranking, and guide conservative fallback heuristics.

skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.

Add: When repository search and file reads return no matches but the bug report names specific files or functions, explicitly mark localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend: (1) checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the supplied patch, (2) surfacing the fact that ranked functions were chosen from the reporter's names rather than repository evidence, and (3) deprioritizing lexical matches until the snapshot/patch is reconciled.

Addendum: when repository searches/reads return no matches but a supplied patch/diff or patch context is present, prefer using the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence (package/module names, file paths, and modified code) and explicitly label any subsequent localization as a 'fallback-to-priors' result if the snapshot and patch disagree.

skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: small presentation helpers that format iterables into human-readable strings commonly implement distinct branches for empty, single-item, and multi-item cases. Reusable bug pattern: the conjunction/separator (joiner) is misplaced because of an incorrect conditional or formatting expression — e.g., returning the joiner for an empty iterable, concatenating joiner onto the single item, or appending the joiner at the end of the full string. Observable signals: minimal repros show (a) empty input returns a non-empty joiner, (b) single-item input has the joiner appended, and (c) final formatted strings place the joiner in the wrong location or with wrong punctuation. Root-location bias: the helper's early 'if not items', 'if len(items) == 1' branches and the final join/format expression (any code that does items = tuple(items); len checks; string concatenation/join/format). Confusable alternatives: upstream splitting/merge bugs or in-place list mutation — disambiguate by running the helper directly on canonical inputs ([], ['x'], ['a','b']). When localizing, inspect all return statements and the exact f-string/join expression; grep for patterns like "len(items) == 1", "joiner", ", '.join(" or return expressions that combine items[-1] and joiner.
anti_patterns: Assuming multi-item formatting issues are caused by upstream splitting rather than the helper's conditional branches.
Trusting a single happy-path return without verifying the empty and single-item branches.
Only looking for index arithmetic/merge loops when the observed signals are string formatting misplacement.

skill.knowledge: Strategy: (1) Open response-routing files (responses.py) and their url bindings (urls.py). (2) Confirm urls.py uses method_dispatch wrappers so response methods are invoked with (request, full_url, headers) and their returned tuple is normalized by BaseResponse.method_dispatch. (3) In each response method, check how the request body is parsed—if the public SDK nests parameters under a wrapper (e.g., CreateApplicationRequest), ensure code extracts that nested dict (params = json.loads(self.body)['CreateApplicationRequest']). (4) Check returned values: ensure handlers return (status, headers, body) or a string that will be normalized, and that 'body' is a JSON string containing the service's top-level envelope keys (e.g., {'ApplicationResponse': {...}} or {'ApplicationsResponse': {'Item': [...]}}) rather than raw model.to_json() objects. (5) Inspect core response helpers (_transform_response/_enrich_response) to see how headers/status/body are normalized. Rank fixes that correct parsing and envelope wrapping above cosmetic renames.

skill.title: project_type_api_wrapper_or_sdk_emulator_v1
skill.trigger: Repo contains 'responses' wrappers and backend model classes (Fake*/Backend) that maintain in-memory collections; issues describe API calls (create/delete/list/describe) that appear to have no effect on subsequent list/describe responses.
skill.knowledge:
Project-type: API emulator / SDK wrapper. Typical structure: a responses layer (HTTP/JSON wrappers) that extracts parameters and forwards to a backend/emulator class which stores in-memory model objects and collections (Fake* or Backend classes). Root-location bias: prioritize backend model files that declare and mutate in-memory collections (e.g., self.account_assignments, self.deleted_account_assignments) and the paired responses functions that call them. Ranking bias: when the problem concerns an API-visible create/delete/list/describe, elevate backend methods that append/remove from model lists and the corresponding response templates/handlers (they often read the same collections). Anti-patterns: treating responses wrappers as the only likely root cause — in emulators the bug frequently lies in the model collection mutation or the way the model is populated/read.

Addendum: In API-emulator projects the responses layer often contains shape/serialization helpers (e.g., AWSServiceSpec._expand in responses.py) that build type/shape dictionaries for request/response envelopes. These helpers are high-value places to inspect when wire shapes are empty/malformed — search for nested expand/expand-like helpers and small proxy/reference classes (names like _RecursiveDictRef).

skill.title: missing_backend_index_or_resource_arn_enumeration_truncation_in_emulator_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when API tag/list/untag calls raise NotFound for resource ARNs even though create/list functions produce resources and tests create snapshots/subnetgroups but subsequent tag/list calls fail.
skill.knowledge: Knowledge: In API-emulator backends, a small helper or index that enumerates known resource ARNs is often used as the canonical existence check for multiple API methods (e.g., list_tags, tag_resource, untag_resource). If that enumeration is accidentally truncated, filtered, or refactored to omit specific collections (snapshots, subnet_groups) then many tag/list/untag APIs will raise NotFound faults for those resource types even though the model objects exist. Root-location bias: inspect (1) backend enumeration helpers and registries (functions named _list_arns/_list_resource_arns/_resource_index), (2) the create/update functions that should register ARNs (create_snapshot/create_subnet_group/create_cluster) and any calls that populate TaggingService, and (3) the shared TaggingService to confirm which ARN keys are present. Confusable alternatives: missing-to_dict fields or serializer omissions can also cause missing wire fields; differentiate by checking whether the model objects and ARNs are present in backend collections. Evidence preference: grep for ARN construction (patterns like f"arn:aws:memorydb:{region}:{account}:snapshot/{name}"), for the enumeration helper body, and for recent edits that removed lines combining multiple collections into the returned list. Ranking bias: elevate fixes that restore correct enumeration/registration of ARNs and ensure create-paths call the tagger/registry above serializer-only fixes.

skill.title: missing_default_for_optional_timestamp_in_constructor_v1
skill.trigger: Reports that a cache/metadata timestamp (change_time/last_used) is None or that cache expiration/last-used behavior fails after object construction or unpickling.
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode: constructors accept an optional timestamp (change_time / last_modified) but do not canonicalize None to a valid timestamp. Observable signals: (1) public field representing time is None at runtime; (2) cache expiry comparisons (p_time <= item.change_time) behave incorrectly; (3) tests that assert last_used ranges or cache trimming fail; (4) pickled cache files load objects whose time fields are None. Root-location bias: constructor (__init__) and any __setstate__/__getstate__ or pickling support. Confusable alternatives: caller intentionally passes None to indicate 'unknown' — confirm call-site semantics (e.g., file_io.get_last_modified() may return None). Anti-patterns: leaving textual/temporal fields set to None, only assigning last_used in callers but not ensuring constructor invariants, and ignoring pickle.load bypass of __init__. Durable guidance: default timestamp parameters inside constructors (e.g., if change_time is None: change_time = time.time()); also initialize last_used explicitly (prefer time.time() for last_used). When objects are pickled/unpickled, add __setstate__/__getstate__ or post-load normalization to ensure timestamps are valid (or document that pickled objects may have None). Prefer fixes that make the object invariant (valid timestamp stored) rather than relying on defensive callers.

edit_history.rationale: This case shows a reusable defect pattern: optional timestamp parameters left as None instead of being defaulted in constructors, causing cache expiration/last-used/pickling problems. Existing fault-mode candidates talk about wrapper textual defaults or mutated collections but not the timestamp/pickling combination. Creating a focused fault-mode skill prevents mixing unrelated subpatterns.

skill.trigger: Issue mentions None/NULL timestamps, broken cache expiry, inconsistent last_used, or failing module pickling/restore flows.
skill.knowledge: Strategy: When a report mentions None timestamps, cache-expiry misbehaviour, or pickling anomalies, prioritize: (1) open the class constructor (__init__) and check how optional timestamp/change_time parameters are handled (look for change_time=None in signature and whether code canonicalizes it, e.g., if change_time is None: change_time = time.time()); (2) grep callers that construct the object (factory/try_to_save_module) to see what values are passed (file_io.get_last_modified() can yield None); (3) inspect persistence code (pickle.dump/load and __getstate__/__setstate__) because pickle.load can bypass __init__ and leave invariants unset; (4) check uses of the timestamp (cache expiration comparisons, last_used updates, garbage-collection cutoffs) to confirm symptom propagation; (5) prefer fixes that restore object invariants inside constructors or in post-unpickle normalization rather than patching scattered callers. Ranking bias: prefer constructor and serialization code over higher-level consumers when timestamps are central to the bug. Anti-pattern to avoid: stopping at the site that compares timestamps (symptom) instead of repairing the constructor/serialization invariant.

Existing strategy candidates focused on wrapper textual defaults; this case adds the distinct, reusable strategy of checking optional timestamp parameters and pickling interactions. skill.title: project_type_parser_or_compiler_frontend_incremental_diff_parser_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when a parser frontend implements an incremental/diff reparse (SequenceMatcher/opcodes) and the bug report mentions insert/delete confusion, incorrect results for small insertions, or when grepping shows many 'DiffParser', 'get_opcodes', '_diff_tokenize', or _NodesTree references.
skill.knowledge:
Project-type lesson: Incremental/diff-based parser modules form a brittle boundary: (1) opcode dispatch (the update loop that reads SequenceMatcher.get_opcodes()) decides whether to copy from the old tree or reparse ranges — a small mistake (treating 'insert' like 'replace') changes the parse-range and can turn insertions into deletions; (2) the tokenizer adapter that produces tokens for a limited until_line (e.g., _diff_tokenize) must agree with the chosen until_line bounds and with the node-copying helpers; (3) node-copy/merge helpers (_NodesTree.copy_nodes/_copy_nodes/_update_insertion_node and add_parsed_nodes/_remove_endmarker) are responsible for prefix concatenation and position updates and are high-risk when opcodes or ranges are wrong.

Evidence preference: when issues mention incremental parsing or patches, prioritize reading the opcode dispatch in the update method first, then the tokenizer adapter that accepts a limited range, and finally node-copy/copy_nodes paths. Confusable alternatives like pure tokenizer bugs can be ruled out by checking whether the update loop computes j1/j2/until_line differently for different opcodes and by comparing actual comments/intent versus implemented code around opcode handling (e.g., comment describing insert-specific narrower parse range but code treating insert like replace).

edit_history.rationale: This repository exposes a distinct, reusable project-type: an incremental/diff-based parser where opcode dispatch, tokenizer-adapter, and node-copy/merge helpers form the brittle boundary. Existing 'parser_or_compiler_frontend' skills cover position propagation and split/merge helpers, but this pattern focuses on 'diff' incremental parsing and opcode-handling; it is a separate, reusable subpattern and warrants a new skill.

skill.title: fault_mode_diff_opcode_misdispatch_insert_as_replace_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when a diff/incremental parser mis-handles small insertions (reports 'insert' vs 'delete' confusion) or when code shows identical handling for 'insert' and 'replace' in opcode dispatch (SequenceMatcher/get_opcodes loop).
skill.knowledge: Fault-mode lesson: When opcode dispatch treats 'insert' like 'replace' the chosen parse bounds (until_line/j2) become too large or incorrectly anchored for insert cases. Consequences: tokenizer adapter receives wrong until_line and yields tokens/ENDMARKER at wrong positions; node-copying may copy wrong ranges or drop necessary prefix/newline adjustments; positions and prefixes propagate incorrectly, making inserts look like deletions or generating parser errors. skill.title: Detect swallowed filesystem exceptions that omit cleanup and produce silent failures
skill.trigger: Triggered when issue text describes permission/IO errors being 'silently ignored', missing warnings, or missing cleanup/garbage-collection after a failed filesystem operation.
skill.knowledge: When reports describe silent filesystem failures or missing cleanup, treat that as a two-part signal: (1) a try/except may be swallowing a PermissionError/OSError without surfacing a user-facing warning or log, and (2) the except branch may omit required cleanup or lock updates. Prioritize locating: filesystem write helpers (save_to_file_system, open/write/pickle calls), surrounding try/except/else/finally structure, explicit cleanup functions (clear_cache, clear_inactive_cache, _remove_cache_and_update_lock), and warning/logging calls. Prefer fixes that either propagate or clearly log the failure (use UserWarning or LOG.warning) and ensure cleanup/lock-update runs in except or finally so on-disk state stays consistent. Confusable alternatives: code that intentionally degrades silently (documented fallback) — differentiate by checking for explicit comments or documented fallbacks. Anti-pattern: treating a bare 'except PermissionError: pass' or warnings.warn(..., Warning) as acceptable without explicit rationale.

edit_history.rationale: This case demonstrates a broadly reusable principle: swallowed filesystem exceptions combined with missing cleanup lead to silent failures and stale state. No close existing general skill captures both the suppressed warning-class misuse and omitted cleanup together, so a new general principle is warranted.

Description: presentation or framing helpers may accidentally swap the order of returned or yielded elements (e.g., returning (right, content) instead of (content, right)), invert boolean/step polarity (e.g., step sign or 'right' flag), or miscompute slice endpoints (off-by-one) — all of which change which glyphs become content vs border or reverse/garble frame sequences. skill.title: parser_or_compiler_frontend_tokenizer_version_sensitive_operator_set_v1
skill.trigger: Triggered when issue text reports language-version-specific syntax being incorrectly accepted (e.g., 'backticks parse', 'old except syntax accepted', 'long-int L suffix accepted', or tests that parametrize per-version semantics).
skill.knowledge: Project-type lesson: In parser/lexer front-ends, the canonical enforcement point for language-version token differences is the token-collection factory (a function that builds/compiles operator and token regexes and returns a TokenCollection cached per version). When a newer grammar should reject deprecated syntax but it is accepted, check for: (1) Operator/Funny/PseudoToken regexes that include deprecated characters or suffixes (backtick, long-int suffix L/l, old octal forms), (2) use of _all_string_prefixes / endpats that may not filter prefixes by version, and (3) the version-keyed token cache getter (e.g., _get_token_collection) to ensure version_info is applied. Evidence preference: open the token-collection factory first, grep for literal deprecated tokens in Operator and number/string patterns, and then confirm tests/fixtures show per-version expectations (test files or conftest). Confusable alternatives: grammar/normalizer rules can also accept deprecated forms, but token-level acceptance is a high-confidence root when the Operator/Number regexes literally include deprecated tokens. Ranking bias: prioritize token-collection construction and its cached retrieval before editing parser/normalizer code.

edit_history.rationale: Existing parser/front-end project_type skills cover incremental parsing and position propagation. This case reveals a distinct, reusable subpattern: version-aware tokenizer construction (the token-collection factory) is a canonical boundary where language-version differences are enforced. That knowledge is reusable across parser front-ends and should be a separate project_type skill.

skill.knowledge: Strategy: For parser frontends, if syntax that should be invalid for a given language version is accepted, do the following in order: (1) Open the token-collection factory function and locate Operator, Number, Funny, and PseudoToken pattern definitions; grep for literal deprecated tokens/suffixes (e.g., '`', 'L' suffix in numbers, old octal patterns). Ranking bias: place tokenizer token-collection and version-cache checks above parser rule edits for version-related acceptance problems.

skill.knowledge:
Project-type: API emulator / SDK wrapper. Typical structure: a responses layer (HTTP/JSON wrappers) that extracts parameters and forwards to a backend/emulator class which stores in-memory model objects and collections (Fake* or Backend classes). Root-location bias: prioritize backend model files that declare and mutate in-memory collections (e.g., self.account_assignments, self.deleted_account_assignments) and the paired responses functions that call them. Ranking bias: when the problem concerns an API-visible create/delete/list/describe, elevate backend methods that append/remove from model lists and the corresponding response templates/handlers (they often read the same collections). Anti-patterns: treating responses wrappers as the only likely root cause — in emulators the bug frequently lies in the model collection mutation or the way the model is populated/read.

Addendum: In API-emulator projects the responses layer often contains shape/serialization helpers (e.g., AWSServiceSpec._expand in responses.py) that build type/shape dictionaries for request/response envelopes. These helpers are high-value places to inspect when wire shapes are empty/malformed — search for nested expand/expand-like helpers and small proxy/reference classes (names like _RecursiveDictRef).

Confusable alternatives: grammar/normalizer rules can also accept deprecated forms, but token-level acceptance is a high-confidence root when the Operator/Number regexes literally include deprecated tokens. Ranking bias: prioritize token-collection construction and its cached retrieval before editing parser/normalizer code.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.

Add: When repository search and file reads return no matches but the bug report names specific files or functions, explicitly mark localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend: (1) checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the supplied patch, (2) surfacing the fact that ranked functions were chosen from the reporter's names rather than repository evidence, and (3) deprioritizing lexical matches until the snapshot/patch is reconciled.

Addendum: when repository searches/reads return no matches but a supplied patch/diff or patch context is present, prefer using the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence (package/module names, file paths, and modified code) and explicitly label any subsequent localization as a 'fallback-to-priors' result if the snapshot and patch disagree.

Addendum (missing-file/fallback behavior): When file reads or greps fail to find a reporter-named file/function but the bug report names a concrete module/path (or a patch/patch_context is supplied), explicitly mark the final localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result in the summary and UI. Prefer any supplied patch paths/contents as primary evidence in that case and surface a short rationale to the user (e.g., 'file not present in snapshot — ranked function chosen from report names / supplied patch').

When a supplied patch/diff is present but the checkout/search returns no matching files, prefer the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence and explicitly label the final localization output as 'fallback-to-priors' (e.g., 'file not present in snapshot — ranked function chosen from supplied patch').
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

skill.title: Handle empty-repo-search and retrieval-fallback bias
skill.trigger: Triggered when repository searches (grep/file-lists) return no matches for expected symbols or when retrieval ranks lexical/parser matches highly despite strong project-architecture signals (e.g., backend/emulator classes, fake-model types, packaging metadata).
skill.knowledge:
If repository search is unexpectedly empty or sparse, explicitly treat that as an operational signal rather than a neutral outcome. Actions: (1) Check packaging, manifests, and patch/diff metadata or alternate snapshots to confirm missing files. (2) If the issue names functions or APIs, treat those names as high-evidence but annotate that evidence as coming from external priors. (3) Reduce weight of generic lexical/parser-front matches when concrete project-architecture signals exist (e.g., backend classes, fake-model types, or emulator patterns). (4) Prefer inspecting packaging/layout or the provided patch before promoting high-confidence localization when search is empty. (5) Make any fallback-to-priors explicit in ranking output so downstream decisions are transparent.

When repo searches return no relevant files but the issue names concrete classes/APIs or describes a patch (e.g., 'removed inheritance from BaseImage'), explicitly treat the naming as an external prior: (a) surface that the localization is a fallback based on the reported symbol rather than repository evidence, and (b) reduce weight of lexical matches from the snapshot while recommending checking packaging/patch metadata or alternate snapshots first.

When repository searches return no matching files and localization ranking is produced from external priors, explicitly annotate output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend re-checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the provided patch before treating ranked functions as code-evidence.

Add: When repository search and file reads return no matches but the bug report names specific files or functions, explicitly mark localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result and recommend: (1) checking packaging/manifest/alternate snapshots or the supplied patch, (2) surfacing the fact that ranked functions were chosen from the reporter's names rather than repository evidence, and (3) deprioritizing lexical matches until the snapshot/patch is reconciled.

Addendum: when repository searches/reads return no matches but a supplied patch/diff or patch context is present, prefer using the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence (package/module names, file paths, and modified code) and explicitly label any subsequent localization as a 'fallback-to-priors' result if the snapshot and patch disagree.

Addendum (missing-file/fallback behavior): When file reads or greps fail to find a reporter-named file/function but the bug report names a concrete module/path (or a patch/patch_context is supplied), explicitly mark the final localization output as a 'fallback-to-priors' result in the summary and UI. Prefer any supplied patch paths/contents as primary evidence in that case and surface a short rationale to the user (e.g., 'file not present in snapshot — ranked function chosen from report names / supplied patch').

When a supplied patch/diff is present but the checkout/search returns no matching files, prefer the patch paths and patch contents as primary evidence and explicitly label the final localization output as 'fallback-to-priors' (e.g., 'file not present in snapshot — ranked function chosen from supplied patch').
anti_patterns: Confidently localizing to lexical/parser matches when repository search finds no relevant files.
Failing to consult patch/packaging metadata when the working snapshot is incomplete.
Overweighting fallback priors without surfacing that fallback to the user or downstream ranking components.

skill.title: fault_mode_missing_public_attribute_initialization_in_wrapper_v1
skill.trigger: Reports of TypeError from string operations in parser/tree code or issue text mentioning None/prefix/indent errors in parser wrappers; diffs that set public attributes to None or change default types in __init__.
skill.knowledge:
Fault mode: wrapper/initializer leaves public or tree-facing fields uninitialized or set to None (or otherwise wrong type) instead of canonical defaults (e.g., '' for textual prefixes, 0/[] for counters/lists). Observable signals: TypeError on string concatenation/slicing in tree traversal methods, grep matches for `prefix` assignments, patch diffs that change __init__ assignments for module/prefix/indents. Root-location bias: wrapper class __init__ and reset/constructor helpers; symptom-location bias: tree methods that concatenate prefixes (e.g., _remove_endmarker, finish, add_parsed_nodes). Confusable alternatives: upstream tokenizer producing unexpected empty prefix — confirm by inspecting token objects and their `prefix` fields. Anti-patterns: setting textual defaults to None, reusing other object's attribute directly without validating its type.

Add: Also watch for wrappers that should forward or expose underlying parser public fields (e.g., self.stack). A missing forward/assignment in __init__ (or not exposing a property delegating to an internal parser) will produce AttributeError at use sites even if internal parser instances are later created.

Add: When a wrapper implements attribute delegation (e.g., via __getattr__) a missing/wrong initializer for the delegate (e.g., assigning self._stream = None or omitting assignment) will surface as AttributeError at call sites — prioritize checking wrapper __init__ and recent diffs that touch the delegated field.

Add: For wrapper/initializer faults, watch textual wrapper fields (prefix, _prefix_remainder, EndMarker-related state). Missing or non-string defaults (or subtle BOM branches that mutate prefix length) will lead to concatenation or off-by-one errors later; verify wrapper __init__/_reset set textual fields to '' (not None) and review EndMarker/prefix-splitting code paths.

edit_history.rationale: The primary defect mechanism is an initializer assigning None (wrong type/default) to fields used for string ops. This is a distinct, reusable fault-mode pattern not represented by the matched fault skills (which focused on boolean coercion or state cleanup). Create a new fault-mode skill describing this mechanism and observable signals.

skill.title: presentational_character_transformation_and_ansi_sequence_mishandling
skill.trigger: Triggered by reports of inserted spaces between characters, filtered/converted uppercase letters, or cursor moving in the wrong direction/column.
skill.knowledge:
Fault-mode: presentational_character_transformation_and_ansi_sequence_mishandling

Trigger: Reported symptoms include unexpected spacing between characters, letters being filtered or case-changed, and incorrect cursor movement or wrong ANSI sequences (cursor moves down instead of up, off-by-one column).

Knowledge: These symptoms commonly arise from two helper-level mistakes in terminal/renderer libraries: (1) string/sequence helper functions that mistakenly convert or filter characters (e.g., generators that only yield lowered uppercase characters or return the wrong iterator), or wrong use of join/concatenation that introduces separators where none were intended; and (2) incorrect assembly of ANSI CSI sequences or wrong numeric parameter arithmetic (off-by-one terminal column adjustments, concatenating integer params incorrectly in f-strings) in a tty/adapter module. When both appear together, treat them as separate but co-located causes: check sequence-processing helpers (strip/mark/join functions) for filtering/transformations, and check terminal adapter functions (cols(), _ansi_escape_sequence, factory_cursor_up, carriage_return) for parameter formatting and sign/direction errors.

Root-location bias: small utilities that compose frames or return flattened character sequences (cells, joiners, strip functions) and terminal adapter modules that build CSI sequences and compute columns. Confusable alternatives: font/terminal rendering bugs or external terminal emulators — prefer code-level fixes if helpers or ANSI factories are present in the repo or patch.

This combination is common in terminal/renderer libraries and deserves its own fault-mode skill rather than being folded into broader presentational skills.
